dw-service.title: DWService Singleton
dw-service.subtitle: Threaded SQLite for Godot 4.5+, registered for you
dw-service.summary: Owns the SQLite connection pool, the write queue and the schema cache. The addon registers it as the DataWiz singleton, so there is no autoload to add.
highlights: No setup: the extension registers a DataWiz singleton and opens the database named in Project Settings the first time anything uses it.
Writes are queued on one thread and batched into transactions; values are read from your objects on the calling thread, so the writer never touches a Godot object.
Reads lease a connection from a pool, and nested records are rehydrated in batches — one query per table per level, not one per reference.

usage.title: There is no step one
usage.description: Drop `addons/datawiz/` into the project. `DataWiz` resolves from any script, and the database at `datawiz/database/path` opens on first use.
usage.code:
func _ready() -> void:
    DataWiz.sql_error.connect(func(context, message):
        push_error("[DataWiz] %s: %s" % [context, message]))
    print(DataWiz.db_connected())   # already true, unless auto_open is off

usage.title: Save slots, when you want control
usage.description: Turn `datawiz/database/auto_open` off and open the file yourself.
usage.code:
func load_slot(n: int) -> void:
    DataWiz.open("user://slot_%d.db" % n, 4)   # path, reader pool size

usage.title: Reads bind their values
usage.description: The WHERE clause is raw SQL by design, but it takes `?` placeholders — player input never reaches the statement text. ORDER BY is checked against the table's own columns.

usage.title: Big reads off the main thread
usage.description: `select_async` runs on a worker thread against a pooled connection and delivers the rows back on the main thread.

usage.title: Batches and durability
usage.code:
DataWiz.save_many(party, true)   # one transaction, one wait
DataWiz.flush()                  # wait for everything queued
DataWiz.checkpoint()             # flush, then fold the WAL back into the file
usage.description: Waiting per record would put each one in its own transaction.

signals.name: connected
signals.description: Emitted after `open()` succeeds and the reader pool is ready.

signals.name: disconnecting
signals.description: Fired when `close()` begins; autoloads save here, and SCRATCH tables are emptied just after.

signals.name: disconnected
signals.description: Emitted once every connection has closed.

signals.name: sql_error
signals.description: Any SQL failure, marshalled to the main thread as (context, message).

signals.name: schema_changed
signals.description: A migration added columns to an existing table: (table, added_columns). Connect this to backfill them.

signals.name: select_completed
signals.description: A select_async finished: (request_id, rows), on the main thread.

methods.name: open(relative_db_path: String, reader_pool_size: int = 4) -> bool
methods.description: Creates the WAL-backed database if needed, spawns the writer thread, and builds the reader pool. Returns `true` on success.

methods.name: close()
methods.description: Gracefully shuts down threads, drains queued writes, and emits `disconnecting`/`disconnected`.

methods.name: db_connected() -> bool
methods.description: Quick status check for scenes that should delay initialization until the DB is online.

methods.name: enqueue_write(sql: String, params: Array = [])
methods.description: Queues a parameterized statement for the writer thread to run asynchronously.

methods.name: write_sync(sql: String) -> bool
methods.description: Executes a write on the writer thread and blocks until it finishes—handy for migrations and tests.

methods.name: log_tuning_snapshot()
methods.description: Logs WAL/cache settings so you can audit tuning decisions in the editor output.

methods.name: get_last_error() -> String
methods.description: Returns the last SQLite error encountered by the service.

methods.name: create_table(table_name: String, definition: Dictionary) -> bool
methods.description: Builds a table from a dictionary of column definitions without needing a DWRecord resource.

methods.name: register_table(record: DWRecord)
methods.description: Caches schema metadata extracted from a DWRecord prototype so queries and migrations can run.

methods.name: select(record: DWRecord, where_clause: String = "", limit: int = -1, order_by: String = "") -> Array
methods.description: Hydrates new DWRecord instances from the backing table using optional filtering helpers.

methods.name: query(sql: String, params: Dictionary = {}) -> Array
methods.description: Runs an ad-hoc SELECT and returns dictionaries; perfect for joins or aggregates.

methods.name: query_record(schema: GDScript, sql: String, params: Dictionary = {}) -> Array
methods.description: Executes custom SQL and hydrates DWRecord-derived resources using the provided schema type.

tips: Call `log_tuning_snapshot()` in development builds to see WAL, cache, and pragma values.
Use `db_connected()` inside `_ready()` when other Autoloads depend on the database before booting.

dw-record.title: DWRecord Resource
dw-record.subtitle: A Resource that knows how to store itself
dw-record.summary: Subclass it and every script variable becomes a column. Nested records are stored in their own table and come back with their parent.
highlights: Every script variable becomes a column; prefix one with an underscore to keep it out of the database.
Adding a variable to a class you have already shipped is handled: the table is diffed and the column added, then schema_changed tells you to backfill it.
A record held by another is saved as its own row linked by owner_guid, and two references to the same row rehydrate as one instance.

usage.title: Declare a record
usage.description: Every script variable becomes a column, exported or not. The variables listed first configure storage and are read as metadata, not stored.
usage.code:
class_name Npc extends DWRecord

var table_name := "npc"           # optional; defaults to the class name
var unique_fields := ["name"]     # optional; defaults to the generated guid
var index_fields := ["faction"]

var name: String = ""
var age: int = 0
var faction: String = "neutral"
var position: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO
var stats: Dictionary = {}
var inventory: Array[Item] = []   # nested records get their own rows

usage.title: Save and load
usage.description: Writes are queued on the writer thread; pass true to block until the row is committed. Every record carries a 16-byte guid generated on construction.
usage.code:
var npc := Npc.new()
npc.name = "Borin"
npc.age = 51
npc.save_to_db()          # queued, returns false only if no database is open
npc.save_to_db(true)      # blocks until committed

var same := Npc.new()
same.load_from_db(npc.get_guid())    # fills this instance in place

usage.title: Nested records
usage.description: A record held by another is written to its own table with owner_guid set, and comes back with its parent. Two references to the same row rehydrate as one instance.
usage.code:
npc.inventory = [sword, potion]
npc.save_to_db(true)                       # writes npc, sword and potion

var loaded := DataWiz.select(Npc.new())    # inventory is populated
var kids := DataWiz.select_children(npc, Item.new())

methods.name: save_to_db(wait: bool = false) -> bool
methods.description: Writes this record, inserting or updating on its unique columns, and saves any nested records with it. Values are read on the calling thread, so the record is safe to modify immediately afterwards.

methods.name: load_from_db(guid: PackedByteArray = PackedByteArray()) -> bool
methods.description: Loads the row with this guid into this instance, leaving your object identity intact. Omit the guid to reload the record's own.

methods.name: delete_from_db(wait: bool = false, cascade: bool = true) -> bool
methods.description: Deletes this record's row; with cascade, rows in every table whose owner_guid points at it go too.

methods.name: get_key() -> String
methods.description: The composite key built from the unique columns — the value a parent stores in its reference to a nested record.

methods.name: get_guid() -> PackedByteArray
methods.description: The 16-byte UUIDv4 assigned when the record was constructed.

tips: Prefix a variable with an underscore to keep it out of the database.
Adding a variable to a class you have already shipped is handled: the column is added on next use and `schema_changed` tells you to backfill it.
`unique_fields` names that do not match a column are reported and dropped, so a typo does not silently change your primary key.

dw-autoload.title: DWAutoLoad Node
dw-autoload.subtitle: A Node that persists itself as a single row
dw-autoload.summary: Base node for global state that should round-trip through SQLite using the same schema metadata as DWRecord.
highlights: Ideal for inventories, progression flags, or analytics caches that live in Autoload singletons.
Automatically mirrors exported properties into a backing table using the node name as the key.
Supports manual `save_to_db(true)` calls when quitting or before scene transitions.

usage.title: Declare the state
usage.description: Same rules as DWRecord, but the table holds one row. Add it as an autoload and it loads itself when the service connects.
usage.code:
class_name GameState extends DWAutoLoad

var table_name := "game_state"

var chapter: int = 1
var flags: Dictionary = {}
var unlocked: Array[String] = []

usage.title: It saves itself
usage.description: The node loads on ready (or when the service connects) and saves on `disconnecting`, so a normal shutdown persists it with no explicit call. Save by hand before anything risky.

methods.name: save_to_db(wait: bool = false) -> bool
methods.description: Persists the node's state to its single row.

methods.name: load_from_db() -> bool
methods.description: Loads the stored row back into this node.

tips: Add it as an autoload; it hooks the service's connect and disconnect signals itself.
`table_type` is always AUTOLOAD for these, which is what makes the table single-row.
